Recall@3 rises from v1 to v2 because v2 retrieves three documents and v1 only one; recall@1 is identical. The retrieval ablation in `results/retrieval_ablation.json` keeps K fixed and changes only the weighting: over the {{abl.n_cases}} answerable cases at top 3, overlap reaches recall@1 {{abl.retrievers.overlap.recall_at_1|.4f}}, recall@3 {{abl.retrievers.overlap.recall_at_3|.4f}} and MRR@3 {{abl.retrievers.overlap.mrr_at_3|.4f}}, idf reaches {{abl.retrievers.idf.recall_at_1|.4f}}, {{abl.retrievers.idf.recall_at_3|.4f}} and {{abl.retrievers.idf.mrr_at_3|.4f}}. On this corpus idf weighting does not beat plain overlap; the gain is K.
